# `gcp.network`

Manages a VPC network or legacy network resource on GCP.

[compute](README.md) · [all services](../README.md)

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Service | compute |
| Scope | global |
| Asset type | `compute.googleapis.com/Network` |
| Tier | 1 (ruled: All four hooks are the Terraform provider's bookkeeping. None of them changes what GCP receives for a configuration written in GCP's own fields, which is why this ships.
post_create (compute_network_delete_default_route.tmpl) is gated on `delete_default_routes_on_create`, a Terraform-only convenience field with no counterpart in the compute API. When true it lists routes matching the network with destRange 0.0.0.0/0 and deletes them. We do not offer that field, so the hook has nothing to fire on.
encoder and update_encoder (compute_network.go.tmpl) do two things. They map `bgp_always_compare_med` and `delete_bgp_always_compare_med` -- again Terraform-only fields -- onto routingConfig.bgpAlwaysCompareMed, the real API field, which a user here sets directly. Then they `delete(obj, "numeric_id")`, removing a Terraform-only computed field from the body; we never put one there.
decoder (compute_network.go.tmpl) is one line: it copies res["id"] into res["numericId"] before Terraform rewrites `id` into its own path-shaped identifier. We do not rewrite ids, so there is nothing to preserve.
THE BOUNDED GAP, and it is deliberate: there is no `delete_default_routes_on_create`. A network created here keeps the default routes GCP gives it, which is GCP's own behaviour; deleting them is a separate act. The BGP convenience pair is likewise absent -- set routingConfig.bgpAlwaysCompareMed, and to clear it send the field explicitly rather than dropping it, because updateMask never removes what a request omits.
) |
| Mutation timeout | 600s |
